doc.title: Peter Appleyard interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 4, 2012

title: Sinatra on the hardship of the big band era
summary: Sinatra told him about touring on buses and 64 one-nighters, Tommy Dorsey's breathing, and watching Basie.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: That’s something, huh? Anyway and that night Benny was suffering with his slipped disc, he had a bad disc, as you know. And the next night Frank came up to me and he said, “Peter,” he said, “Benny came last night and he didn’t come back to say hello.” I said, “no, Frank, he enjoyed the show so much but he was in such pain.” And then he opened up to me, Frank did, about the big band era and what it was like and how tough it was for those band leaders. He said, “I really have great respect for them.” He said, “because we’d be traveling on buses with broken seats and engines that kept breaking down, and they’d do 64 consecutive one-nighters.” And then he got talking about watching Tommy [Dorsey] breathing. You know all that about the circular breathing. And tell me about how he used to swim a lot under water. It was really wonderful, because they asked you not to bother him if he came on stage. Nine times out of ten he would be in the wings digging Basie. He’d say “Shiny Stocking, Shiny Stocking.” And then some nights they’d open up the band and Basie would open it, and Sinatra would be conducting. And people didn’t know who it was until he turned around you know. Then
one night he saw the music stands and they said CB on there, he came out and said, “Charlie Barnet!”
